To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
use of TMT reduces errors in antibody identification by 30--62% and enhances learning of antibody identification by 87-- 93%.

1) the use of expert systems technology can enhance both the teaching of and performance by medical technology students in the area of antibody identification and 2) the use of an expert system can enhance the performance of medical technologists in the same area.

use of an expert-system-based computerized tutor for teaching antibody identification to medical technology students was found to be effective in enhancing learning, and use of a similar tutor by practicing medical technoloigsts was found to be effecitve in reducing errors in antibody identification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computer-based system to assist in teaching and practicing a complex problem-solving activity in transfusion medicine.
the development of an expert-system shell that provides a framework for the development and use of expert-system-based teaching and problem-solving tools in transfusion medicine.
the use of artificial intelligence techniques in the development of a system that can be used to teach students or to provide assistance to practitioners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TMT is an effective tool for teaching students and for providing support to practitioners in the field of transfusion medicine.
the use of TMT can improve the accuracy of medical technologists and the quality of their work, and that it can enhance student learning.
the TMT is a useful tool in both teaching and practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
expert system technology has been successfully applied to the teaching and practice of antibody identification.
the expert-system technology is effective in reducing errors and in improving learning.
the TMT is a useful tool for the training of students and for providing assistance to practitioners.
The main takeaway from our work is that
expert-system technology can be successfully used to improve performance in a complex task and also to teach students to perform that task.
expert-system technology can be used to teach and support practitioners.
a computer system designed to monitor and provide suggestions during problem-solving tasks can be used to enhance learning, and to improve the performance of practicing professionals.
